children: British government bond ⁠yields fell on Friday after surging to multi-decade highs a day earlier as signs of recovering Middle Eastern energy supplies helped oil prices to cool.
The yield on 2-year gilts (GB2YT=RR) slumped by 12 basis points to the lowest since September 10 at 4.6882%, on course for the biggest daily fall since September 16.
Ten-year gilt yields (GB10YT=RR), which hit their highest since 2007 on Thursday, fell as ​low ‌as 5.323%, down 6 bps, with similar sized ‌moves in the five-year yield.
The 30-year yield (GB30YT=RR) was down 6 bps, a day after surpassing 6% for the first time since 1998.
